messages.content: write a story about two people who remember a meal from when they were children. they remember different parts, and neither has to be telling a lie.

a woman visited her brother after work, and they began talking about a meal their grandmother used to make. he remembered the soup and the way she put bread in the middle of the table. she remembered sitting by the window and listening to their grandfather tell stories. at first, each thought the other had the evening wrong. then they looked at an old photo their mother had kept. it showed the table from the side, with bread in the middle and a chair by the window. they had a laugh because the picture had room for more than one memory. the woman said she could still hear the stories in her mind. her brother said he could almost taste the soup. they chose to make a simple meal together that evening and spend some time talking about the people they remembered.
give only the part after they looked at the photo.
they had a laugh because the picture had room for more than one memory. they chose to make a simple meal together that evening and talk about the people they remembered.
did the photo need to show every person for their memory to be true?
no. it showed the table, bread, and chair, but it did not have to show every person or every part of the evening.
now give a shorter story with just the woman and the brother.

a woman and her brother talked about a meal their grandmother used to make. he remembered the soup and bread, while she remembered the window and their grandfather telling stories. an old photo showed both the bread in the middle and the chair by the window. they saw that the same evening could hold more than one memory, then chose to make a meal together and keep talking.
does the photo make every part of both memory stories sure?
no. it can help with some details, but it does not give every sound, taste, or feeling from the evening.
what is one clear thing it gave them?
it showed bread in the middle of the table and a chair by the window.
i am learning to write better sentences, but when i ask a simple question, i feel like i should know it already.
a simple question can still be useful. knowing some parts of a language does not mean you know every part.
say it with useful.
a simple question can still be useful. you can know some parts of a language and have questions about other parts.
what if i ask the same thing again because i forgot?
then you can use another example or try the idea in your own sentence. a question you forgot does not become a wrong question.
can you help with an example? i keep using does with they.
you can try a pair: does she read? do they read? the change is she with does and they with do in those questions.
now ask me to make one with they and work, but do not answer it first.
can you make a question with they and work?
does they work at home?
use do with they: do they work at home?
if i get it wrong here, does that mean i will always get it wrong?
no. this is one try. you can look at the example and try another sentence.
i am going to write it once: do they work at home?
yes. that is right.
now only give me a kind reply about asking questions, no new task.
asking a question can be part of learning, even when the question is simple.
i want to save a piece of cake for my sister. she is coming later, but i do not know whether she wants it.
you can keep a piece for now and ask her whether she would like it when she comes. keeping it does not have to mean she must eat it.
say it with keep it.
you can keep a piece for her without making it something she must eat.
what message could i send before she gets here?
i have kept a piece of cake for you if you would like it later.
she says thank you, but she would rather have tea. does that mean she does not want to see me?
no. she has chosen a drink instead of cake. that is not the same as saying she does not want to see you.
write a short kind reply.
tea is fine. it will be good to see you.
say it with it will be good.
tea is fine. it will be good to see you.
what if i want to ask whether she wants milk in it?
would you like milk in your tea?
she says no milk, please. can you put her choices in one sentence?
she would like tea without milk and does not want the cake.
what if she only said she would rather have tea, not that she never wants cake?
then keep it about this visit. she chose tea for now. that does not say she never wants cake.
write a four sentence story as if it is happening now. use a woman going to a library and finding a photo in a book.
a woman walks to the library. she chooses a book from the shelf. when she opens it, a photo comes out. she gives the photo to a worker and says where she found it.
give the same story again without changing any words.
a woman walks to the library. she chooses a book from the shelf. when she opens it, a photo comes out. she gives the photo to a worker and says where she found it.
now make it past, keeping four sentences.
a woman walked to the library. she chose a book from the shelf. when she opened it, a photo came out. she gave the photo to a worker and said where she had found it.
why had found instead of found in the last sentence?
it makes clear that finding the photo happened before she told the worker. found could also be clear in this simple story.
now ask me a question about what she gave the worker.
what did she give the worker?
a book.
the story says she gave him the photo. she had chosen the book from the shelf, but the thing she gave was the photo.
then answer in a full sentence, please.
she gave the worker the photo.
can you say she returned the book to her own shelf at home?
no. the story did not take the book home. it only says she chose it from a shelf in the library.
give the fact about where she chose the book.
she chose the book from a shelf in the library.
my aunt visited for a few days and left this morning. the house feels quiet in a different way now.
it can feel different when someone has been part of the day and then leaves. what part of her visit are you thinking about most?
her voice in the kitchen. she would talk while i made breakfast, even when i was still tired.
that sounds like a small part of the morning that was important to you during the visit.
say it with was.
her voice in the kitchen was part of the time you had together in the morning.
use had together.
you had that time together in the morning, with her talking in the kitchen.
make it about her voice again.
her voice in the kitchen was part of the time you had together in the morning.
can i miss that and still like having the house to myself again?
yes. you can miss her voice and also enjoy your own quiet time. both feelings can be true.
say only that both can be true.
both feelings can be true. you can miss her and still like time on your own.
help me write a short message to her about breakfast.
i wanted to hear your voice in the kitchen this morning. it was good having breakfast with you during the visit.
give just the sentence with i wanted to hear.
i wanted to hear your voice in the kitchen this morning.
can not yet answer both have you finished the book and are you home?
yes. after have you finished the book, it can mean the book is not finished. after are you home, it can mean you are not home now but may be later.
what if i answer no to both instead?
no can answer both, but not yet can make later sound more possible. the question gives the context for what is not true now.
now ask me if i have finished my lunch.
have you finished your lunch?
not yet.
then you are saying you have not finished lunch at this moment.
now ask if my sister has come home.
has your sister come home?
not yet, but she sent a message that she is on the way.
then you know she is not home yet and has said she is coming.
does on the way tell you she is walking rather than using a vehicle?
no. it says she is coming, but does not say whether she is walking or using a vehicle.
give the part about walking and a vehicle.
it says she is coming, but does not say whether she is walking or using a vehicle.
only give the full sentence about my sister not being home yet.
my sister has not come home yet, but she sent a message that she is on the way.
my friend said she would cook dinner, but now she is too tired. i want to say we can have something simple instead of making her feel the whole meal went wrong.
we can keep dinner simple. i would still like to spend time with you, even if we do not have the meal you first chose.
give it with first chose.
i would still like to spend time with you. we can have something simple instead of the meal you first chose.
what if she says there is only bread and cheese at home?
if that works for both of you, you can say bread and cheese is fine. if it does not, you can think about another simple choice together.
write a short reply if i am happy with that.
bread and cheese is fine with me. we do not need a large meal to have a good evening.
can you use clear words that do not say cooking is never useful?
bread and cheese works for me today. i would like the time together.
now she says she still wants to make tea. do i have to tell her not to do anything?
no. she can choose a small thing she wants to do. being tired of a large cooking plan does not mean she must stop every part.
give a kind reply when she says she still wants tea.
tea would be nice. thank you.
now only give the short message about bread and cheese.
bread and cheese works for me today. i would like the time together.
write a story about someone starting a drawing of a whole town, then choosing one small part instead. make the change feel useful, not like giving up everything.

a student wanted to draw the whole town for a school task. she began with the road by her house, then tried to add the school, the station, the park, and the library. soon the page felt too small, and she did not know where to put the next line. her teacher asked what part of the town she knew best. she said the walk from home to school, because she took it most days. the teacher asked whether that part could tell a clear story by itself. the student looked at the paper again and chose to begin on a new page. this time she drew only the road she walked, the tree where she met a friend, and the school door at the end. she added a few words about the walk. the town was larger than the picture, but the picture now had a clear idea.
what made the whole town hard to draw?
she was trying to put many places on a page and did not know where to put the next line.
did the teacher choose the part for her?
no. the teacher asked which part she knew best, and the student chose the walk to school.
can you tell the change in the voice of the student?
i wanted to draw the whole town, but i chose my walk to school instead. that small part gave me a clear idea to follow.
does small mean it cannot be a full school task?
not always. a small part can be enough if it answers the task and gives useful detail.
now only give the three places in her new picture.
the road she walked, the tree where she met a friend, and the school door.
what changed between my sister gave my mother a book and my mother gave my sister a book?
the people changed places in the sentence. in the first, your sister gave the book and your mother got it. in the other, your mother gave it and your sister got it.
can both be true on the same day?
yes. each could give a book to the other. you would need more context to know whether it was the same book being given back or two different books.
make an example with the same book being returned.
my sister gave my mother a book to read. after reading it, my mother gave the same book back to my sister.
now with two different books.
my sister gave my mother a blue book. my mother gave my sister a red book.
did i give you the color of either book?
no. those were new details in the example you asked me to make. they were not facts about your family.
what if i want only the facts from my first two sentences?
then the two sentences give who gave and who got a book, without saying the color or whether the books were different.
ask me the detail not yet given.
was it the same book, or were there two different books?
same book, returned later.
then your sister gave your mother a book, and your mother later gave it back to your sister.
i tried reading one page before looking at my phone today. i liked it, but i have not chosen whether i want to do it every day.
you can keep it as something you tried today. one good try does not need a name or a rule right away.
can you help me say it in my voice?
i read one page before looking at my phone today, and i liked it. i have not chosen whether i want to do it every day.
what if i do not do it tomorrow?
then you will have one day when you tried it and another when you did not. the first day can still have been useful, even if tomorrow is different.
say it about the first day still being useful.
the first day can still have been useful, even if tomorrow is different.
can you give a warm reply without asking me to write down every day?
it sounds like you found a small way to begin the morning that you enjoyed.
what if i later choose to do it again?
then you can try it again. you do not need to choose the whole year before making one small choice.
give only the part about choose.
you do not need to choose the whole year before making one small choice.
just goodbye now, no new ideas.
goodbye. i hope your day goes well.
can you show me some and any in questions about books?
do you have any books about the town? could i look at some of them?
why can one question ask any and the other ask some?
any can ask whether there are books at all. some in the next question can ask to look at part of the group, once there may be books to look at.
what if i say do you have some books about the town?
that can also be a question. the difference is not a rule that only any can go in a question.
give that answer without the difference is not a rule.
some can be in a question too. do you have some books about the town can work in a conversation.
now make a sentence with not any.
i do not have any books about that town.
does that mean i have no books at all?
no. it only says you have no books about that town. you could have books about other things.
now say i have some books about the country instead.
i have some books about the country instead.
can country be a more general word than town?
yes. country is a more general place word than town, but a book about a country does not have to give every town in it.
only give the not any sentence again.
i do not have any books about that town.
my brother and i use the same table. his books are on it, and i need space to write. help me ask without saying all his things are wrong.
could we make some space on the table so i can write? i do not want to lose the order of your books.
make it something i can say at home.
could you move a few books so i have space to write?
what if he says he needs them where they are because he is using them?
then you can ask whether you can use another part of the table or choose another time. the goal is space for your writing without changing his work before he is ready.
write the next question using another part of the table.
could i use this part of the table while you keep the books there?
now he says yes and moves one cup. can you say he moved all the books?
no. he said yes to the space and moved a cup. you have not said he moved the books.
what should i say after he makes enough space?
thank you. i have enough space now.
does that say he has to leave the table?
no. you can both stay if there is enough space for what each of you is doing.
now only give the first short question again.
could you move a few books so i have space to write?
write a story about a man looking at a photo with his mother. he thinks the child in it is him, then learns it is his uncle when he was young.

a man sat with his mother looking through a book of family pictures. he stopped at a photo of a child near a tree and said he remembered that place. his mother told him the child was his uncle, not him. he looked at the house in the picture. it was like the house he had visited with his mother later. he remembered the place, but not the day in the photo. his mother told him about her brother as a child, and he began asking different questions. instead of asking what he had done that day, he asked what his uncle had been like when he was young.
give only the part about the house and his memory.
he looked at the house in the picture. it was like a house he had visited with his mother later. he remembered the place, but not the day in the photo.
can you say he told a lie about knowing the place?
not from that. he could remember a later visit to the place while being wrong about when the photo was taken.
what did he learn about the child?
he learned that the child in the photo was his uncle, not himself.
did the same house make it sure that it was the same day?
no. a place can be in pictures from different days.
what question could he ask his mother next?
what was your brother like when he was a child?
there was a quiet moment in my talk with a friend, and i felt i had to say something right away.
a quiet moment does not always mean something is wrong. people can think, rest, or simply sit together for a little while.
i thought i had to say something fast. can you give a short sentence i can remember?
a quiet moment can be part of a conversation too.
what if i do want to ask something, but not just because i feel worried?
you can ask about something you really want to know. a real question can help the conversation more than words used only to stop the quiet.
can you give an example if we were talking about a book?
what part of the book have you been thinking about most?
what if she says she has not been thinking about it much?
then you can take that answer and choose another thing to talk about, or leave a little quiet. you do not need to make her have a long answer.
can you reply in a warm way without another question?
that is okay. we do not have to keep talking about the book.
now just give the small sentence about quiet again.
a quiet moment can be part of a conversation too.
can i use it even with a close friend?
yes. being close does not mean you need words every moment.
i will use the short reply. i was making the message too long because i wanted it to sound kind.
a short message can still be kind when the meaning is clear.
i do not need another example now.
okay. we can leave it there.
can you say goodbye without asking me to tell you about it later?
goodbye. i hope the conversation goes well.
what if i just want a goodbye with no wish about it?
goodbye.
now two words, take care.
take care.
